lanes.pitch: Open Lolly QR Code, type a web address and download the finished file. It takes a minute, and you need no account and nothing installed.
Lolly opens wearing Lolly Demo, its own sample design system. Give it your colours, fonts and logos once, and every tool wears them from then on.
A certificate, a signature, a calendar file, a print sheet or a card for a link: pick the tool, fill in the fields and download. Each one comes out in your colours and type.
The Assets view holds the files, fonts and colours you add, all in one place. Find a piece again, change the piece and use the same art in any tool.
A sports club, a choir, a local group: set the colours, type and logo once, and everyone's posters, notices and certificates match, with no designer on hand.
Export the design system as one .lolly file and send the file round. Each person who opens the file gets the same colours, type and logos in their own Lolly.
Two people, two devices, one design, edited live. Share an invite across the table and both screens hold the same session: there is no server in the middle.
Send each piece where it was asked for: a link that carries the design, print-true PDF, video or slides, or straight to Discord, Google Drive and the places you already post.

An agency, a studio or a freelancer keeps a design system per client, with that client's logos and fonts inside, and switches as the work changes. Each piece is drawn in the system you chose for the piece.
A partner sent their design system as a .lolly file? Open the file and make the piece in their colours, with their rules, from your own Lolly.
A sponsor's logo on the poster, a joint announcement, a wall of partner marks for the event: the lead brand draws the piece, and the partner's mark goes in as artwork.
Bring finished work in, set the rules once and keep the tools you already use.
A certificate for each name on a list, an agenda for the day, a diagram for the lesson. Fill in the fields once, then make one file per row of a spreadsheet.
Wayfinding signs, a countdown on the big screen, a dressed booth and a sponsor wall, all in the event's colours.
The app and its documentation come in 27 languages, and Certificate has a Language field, so one layout serves every language in the room.
Reduced motion, high contrast, larger text and calmer previews are one switch each, and the file Lolly makes stays the same whichever you choose.
One render path. The app, the terminal and an agent all make the same file.
An open MCP endpoint with no token and no sign-in: list the tools, read a tool's inputs, check them and render the file.
Render on-brand files in CI with the same flags you use at your desk: one file, or one for each row of a CSV.

Agents are first-class users. Anything a person can make in the app, an agent can make through the MCP server or the CLI: the same tools, the same brand rules and the same render path, and each file still records who made the file.
Your organisation runs Lolly Work? Connect the app to its address and sign in. Its tools, design systems and shared projects appear, and your own saves stay yours.
Sign-in with your own identity provider, roles, locked inputs, shared catalogues, approvals and an audit trail, on a Lolly Work server your organisation runs.

A static web host is the easy path, and an air-gapped network takes the same install. Lolly Work, the organisation server, is open source too: run it on Kubernetes, on one machine or with your platform team.

links.label: Run your own Lolly Work server

lanes.pitch: Most data exfiltration is mundane: a confidential file handed to a stranger's website for a ten-second job. Lolly's utilities do those jobs inside the app, with no account and no server in the middle. A file Lolly makes can say who made the file, and Lolly Verify reads that record back.
